The railway compartment scenario formalizes a latent variable estimation problem. Each passenger's response to a random question reveals a noisy projection onto their personal worldview. The shared question acts as a common kernel, inducing dependencies across responses. Maximum likelihood estimation of the latent variable (the passenger's identity) can be achieved by comparing observed responses to role-specific conditional distributions. This yields a structured probabilistic classifier.
